When bluebird bio launched betibeglogene (Zynteglo) for beta-thalassemia at $2.8 million, Massachusetts Medicaid negotiated an outcomes-based contract: the state pays in installments over five years, with refunds if patients do not maintain transfusion independence.
Makers of one-time gene therapies have offered outcomes-based arrangements: payment is spread over several years, and part of it is refunded if the therapy stops working.
Five-year outcome-linked payment reduced Massachusetts Medicaid's upfront liability by approximately 60% while maintaining patient access to the therapy.
Spreading and conditioning payment shifts part of the risk that the therapy fails from the payer to the manufacturer.
